newsitem.title: UK: Manchester United nets another record high.
newsitem.headline: Manchester United nets another record high.

text.p: Shares in Manchester United Plc were booted to a record high for a third day on Thursday as fund managers bought stock in the English premier league club ahead of its entry next week into the FTSE 250 index, analysts said.
The stock was up 26-1/2p to 641-1/2p by 1249 GMT in light volume of 236,490 shares.
"The rise is mainly due to their entry to the FTSE 250, as fund managers try to add it to their portfolios," Paul Stevens, private client manager at brokerage Waters Lunniss.
Manchester United is due to join the index on December 23.
Stevens said the recent wave of soccer teams coming to the market had helped make them an attractive investment.

Nick Knight, head of research at Nomura, said United's success against Austrian champions Rapid Vienna in the European champions competition had boosted the stock, even though the club's domestic performance had fallen short of last year's success.
United is currently sixth in the English Premier league, and is set to play Portuguese league winners Porto next March in the quarter finals of the European champions cup.
